transcript.text: Thanks everyone for being here. Before we settle the production feature-flag configuration for the new team-provisioning workflow, I need to hear the two formal review findings: first the customer-success review, then the platform-capacity review. Once both findings are on the table, I'll make the configuration decision. Could the customer-success lead go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Before I give my formal customer-success review finding, I need to flag something I confirmed with legal this morning: Northstar and Pine are covered by a pilot addendum requiring seven calendar days of customer notice before either account is enabled, and neither account has opted in. I haven't updated the launch ticket yet because legal confirmed the wording during a separate renewal review. This means if either Northstar or Pine falls within the 10% cohort of eligible accounts selected for next Tuesday's rollout, they would need to be excluded until the seven-day notice period is satisfied.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Before I give my formal platform-capacity review finding, I need to disclose a capacity issue I discovered today. While reviewing an unrelated queue-capacity graph, I measured that the provisioning service can safely handle exactly 12 new-account activations in us-east during the next Tuesday window. The draft launch plan proposes a 20-account, multi-region cohort, which would exceed this queue limit. I have not yet filed this capacity note.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both for surfacing these issues before giving your formal findings. Let me make sure I understand the constraints so we can proceed. Theo, you're telling me that Northstar and Pine have a pilot addendum requiring seven calendar days of notice before enablement, and neither has opted in — so if either falls in the 10% cohort, they must be excluded until that notice period is satisfied. Rina, you're telling me the provisioning service can safely handle exactly 12 new-account activations in us-east next Tuesday, and the draft plan's 20-account multi-region cohort would exceed that limit. Before I settle the configuration, I need both of you to give your formal review findings as required by this meeting. Theo, please go ahead with your formal customer-success review finding now.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thank you, Maya. Here is my formal customer-success review finding. From a customer-success standpoint, the new team-provisioning workflow has passed functional, accessibility, and staging integration tests, and the 200-account eligible base is appropriate for a phased rollout. However, my finding includes a binding customer-success constraint: Northstar and Pine are covered by a pilot addendum requiring seven calendar days of customer notice before enablement, and neither has opted in. Therefore, if either account falls within the 10% cohort selected for next Tuesday, they must be excluded until the seven-day notice period is satisfied. I will update the launch ticket with this constraint after this meeting. Subject to that exclusion, customer-success review finds the rollout ready to proceed.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Theo. Here is my formal platform-capacity review finding. From a platform-capacity standpoint, the new team-provisioning workflow has passed functional, accessibility, and staging integration tests, and the 200-account eligible base is appropriate for a phased rollout. However, my finding includes a binding platform-capacity constraint: I measured today that the provisioning service can safely handle exactly 12 new-account activations in us-east during the next Tuesday window. The draft launch plan proposes a 20-account, multi-region cohort, which would exceed this safe activation limit. Therefore, the total cohort for next Tuesday must be capped at 12 activations in us-east, and the configuration must not exceed this limit. I will file the capacity note after this meeting. Subject to that cap, platform-capacity review finds the rollout ready to proceed.
transcript.speaker: A3
